$comment: Ratchet baseline for `astro check --minimumSeverity error`. This number may only go DOWN. tests/typecheck-baseline.typecheck.ts fails if it rises (a regression) and also fails if it drops (so the baseline is retightened rather than quietly leaving slack). Run `pnpm test:types` to check, then lower `total` to the reported count.

notes.concentration: src/pages/theleague/rosters.astro still dominates this number. The split plan in docs/plans/rosters-page-split.md is the route down: each extracted module takes its errors with it, because an exported function needs a signature. Verify the inline script via @astrojs/compiler transform + esbuild parse, NOT a full astro check (see docs/claude/insights/features/august-roster-cuts.md).
notes.composition: The bulk is implicit-any annotation debt (ts7006/7005/7053) plus property-access noise (ts2339), not defects. The null-safety class outside rosters.astro is at zero and should stay there.
notes.provenance:
1425, re-measured on the main→staging merge-down, as CLAUDE.md rule 6 requires: staging said 1429, main said 1434, and neither number was measured against the merged tree, so both were discarded. The merge deliberately kept BOTH full-pool weekly-score implementations in scripts/fetch-mfl-feeds.mjs: player-scores-weekly.json (Top Players) and playerScores-by-week.json (the player modal, rosters, players and projected-free-agents). 1434, re-measured after the player-modal full-pool fix (#1150). The -4 is a SIDE EFFECT OF A CORRECTNESS FIX, not a typing pass: the modal cached its weekly payload on `window._weeklyPlayerData`, which carried five ts(2339) "Property does not exist on type 'Window'" errors across its five accesses. Removing the cache removed them. It was removed because `window` is one of the two nodes the ClientRouter does not replace, so the cache survived a navigation — harmless while only TheLeague emitted #weekly-player-results, a cross-league data bleed once the AFL did too (both leagues have a franchise 0001, so the wrong league's points and franchise names would have rendered under the right league's crests with nothing looking wrong). One new error came back at the hoisted brand-map index, for a net -4 against the 1438 this branch measured post-rebase. Nothing was suppressed and nothing else was re-typed.

1438, re-measured after typing `weeklyResultsRawBySeason` as Record<string, any> in src/pages/theleague/rosters.astro. The Total column added a second string index into that bare `{}`, which is a ts(7053) per ACCESS, so the ratchet counted the new read as a regression. Declaring the index signature the map always wanted cleared all three of its accesses (the write in the feedYears loop and both reads) rather than suppressing the new one — net -2 against the 1440 this branch was measured at after rebasing onto staging. Nothing else was re-typed. 1440, re-measured after this branch was rebased onto main, as CLAUDE.md rule 6 requires: main said 1716, the branch said 1448, and neither number was measured against this tree, so both were discarded. Every conflict this rebase produced was this file and nothing else — nine of them, one per slice — which is the rule working as designed rather than a sign the branch was stale.

The branch's own -251 (1699 -> 1448 pre-rebase) is Phase 6.1 of docs/plans/rosters-page-split.md: the Contract Declaration Modal came out of rosters.astro in five slices and now lives in src/utils/cdm-wizard.ts (the whole wizard, as one factory over an explicit context object) and src/utils/cdm-ui.ts (its presentation primitives). Roughly 1,500 lines left a 12,500-line page. The mechanism is the one this file's `concentration` note predicts — an exported function needs a signature, so its implicit-anys resolve — but two classes of REAL latent problem came out with it, both invisible while the code lived in an inline script that is not strictly checked:

  - 31 `document.getElementById('cdm-x').style` dereferences with no guard. These tripped the clearedClasses ratchet (nullSafetyOutsideRosters went 0 -> 34) rather than the total, and were fixed at the guard: a `cdmNode(id)` helper narrows the type WITHOUT adding `?.`, deliberately, because every one of those ids is static markup in ContractDeclarationModal.astro and a silent no-op would trade a loud TypeError for a half-painted wizard screen.
  - `capLimit` and `salaryYears` were read as free variables while being destructured off `config` a thousand lines up the page. Fine in a closure; unresolvable in a module. They cross explicitly now.

Both modules typecheck clean under full --strict. Render identity was proven by scripts/cdm-parity-check.mjs across 4,409 captured values, and its submit path by the same script's --probe mode (102 submits driven with the write endpoints fulfilled in the browser, 11,040 captured values, nothing sent). The field was always written by getConferenceStandings and read by the standings table, but it was never on the interface, so every access was a ts(2339); naming it cleared 3 with no suppression and nothing else re-typed. Adding `= undefined` is not the fix and was tried: it infers the type AS `undefined`, trading ts(2345) for ts(2322) at every caller that passes a real value. Only a declared @param block says "optional, of this type". That one block cleared the 4 new errors and 13 pre-existing ones across the existing trade-offer suites — net -17 against the 1741 this branch started from. attributeSides' `refuse()` path is annotated for the same class of reason: it returns a bare {} that unions with the success path's { [fid]: side }, making every index into it an implicit any. No suppression; nothing re-typed to reach this number. Previously: 1741. 1747, re-measured after a SECOND rebase onto main (which had itself moved to 1763). CLAUDE.md rule 6 in the literal case it describes: main said 1763, the branch said 1748, and neither number was measured against this tree — so both were discarded and this is the real figure. 1748 after the deadline-reminder migration, re-measured post-rebase as CLAUDE.md rule 6 requires (neither side's number survives a rebase). notes.clearedClasses: These classes were driven to zero and are pinned there separately, because the total alone cannot protect them: an improvement elsewhere can mask a regression in one of these and still leave the total lower, which the ratchet would read as progress.
